1: 1 The words of Koheleth, the son of David, king in Jerusalem. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Vanity of vanities, saith Koheleth; Vanity of vanities, all is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
What profit hath man of all his labour Wherein he laboureth under the sun? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh; And the earth abideth for ever. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The sun also ariseth, And the sun goeth down, And hasteth to his place where he ariseth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The wind goeth toward the south, And turneth about unto the north; It turneth about continually in its circuit, And the wind returneth again to its circuits. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
All the rivers run into the sea, Yet the sea is not full; Unto the place whither the rivers go, Thither they go again. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
All things toil to weariness; Man cannot utter it, The eye is not satisfied with seeing, Nor the ear filled with hearing. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
That which hath been is that which shall be, And that which hath been done is that which shall be done; And there is nothing new under the sun. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Is there a thing whereof it is said: 'See, this is new'?—it hath been already, in the ages which were before us. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

There is no remembrance of them of former times; neither shall there be any remembrance of them of latter times that are to come, among those that shall come after. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I Koheleth have been king over Israel in Jerusalem. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven; it is a sore task that God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised therewith. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and a striving after wind. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
That which is crooked cannot be made straight; And that which is wanting cannot be numbered. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

I spoke with my own heart, saying: 'Lo, I have gotten great wisdom, more also than all that were before me over Jerusalem'; yea, my heart hath had great experience of wisdom and knowledge. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly—I perceived that this also was a striving after wind. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For in much wisdom is much vexation; And he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow. <span class="anchor"
2: 2 I said in my heart: 'Come now, I will try thee with mirth, and enjoy pleasure'; and, behold, this also was vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I said of laughter: 'It is mad'; and of mirth: 'What doth it accomplish?' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

I searched in my heart  ​ how to pamper my flesh with wine, and, my heart conducting itself with wisdom, how yet to lay hold on folly, till I might see which it was best for the sons of men that they should do under the heaven the few days of their life. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I made me gardens and parks, and I planted trees in them of all kinds of fruit; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I made me pools of water, to water therefrom the wood springing up with trees; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

I acquired men-servants and maid-servants, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of herds and flocks, above all that were before me in Jerusalem; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

I gathered me also silver and gold, and treasure such as kings and the provinces have as their own; I got me men-singers and women-singers, and the delights of the sons of men, women very many. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem; also my wisdom stood me in stead. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them; I withheld not my heart from any joy, for my heart had joy of all my labour; and this was my portion from all my labour. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do; and, behold, all was vanity and a striving after wind, and there was no profit under the sun. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness and folly; for what can the man do that cometh after the king? even that which hath been already done. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The wise man, his eyes are in his head; But the fool walketh in darkness. And I also perceived that one event happeneth to them all. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

Then said I in my heart: 'As it happeneth to the fool, so will it happen even to me; and why was I then more wise?' Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

For of the wise man, even as of the fool, there is no remembrance for ever; seeing that in the days to come all will long ago have been forgotten. And how must the wise man die even as the fool! <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
So I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun was grievous unto me; for all is vanity and a striving after wind. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And I hated all my labour wherein I laboured under the sun, seeing that I must leave it unto the man that shall be after me. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And who knoweth whether he will be a wise man or a fool? yet will he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shown myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Therefore I turned about to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labour wherein I had laboured under the sun. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

For there is a man whose labour is with wisdom, and with knowledge, and with skill; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For what hath a man of all his labour, and of the striving of his heart, wherein he laboureth under the sun? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For all his days are pains, and his occupation vexation; yea, even in the night his heart taketh not rest. This also is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy pleasure for his labour. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For who will eat, or who will enjoy, if not I?  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

For to the man that is good in His sight He giveth wisdom, and knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner He giveth the task, to gather and to heap up, that he may leave to him that is good in the sight of God. This also is vanity and a striving after wind. <span class="anchor"
3: 3 To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A time to be born, and a time to die; A time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A time to kill, and a time to heal; A time to break down, and a time to build up; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A time to weep, and a time to laugh; A time to mourn, and a time to dance; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; A time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A time to seek, and a time to lose; A time to keep, and a time to cast away; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A time to rend, and a time to sew; A time to keep silence, and a time to speak; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A time to love, and a time to hate; A time for war, and a time for peace. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
What profit hath he that worketh in that he laboureth? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I have seen the task which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised therewith. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

He hath made every thing beautiful in its time; also He hath set the world in their heart, yet so that man cannot find out the work that God hath done from the beginning even to the end. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I know that there is nothing better for them, than to rejoice, and to get pleasure so long as they live. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
But also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy pleasure for all his labour, is the gift of God. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever; nothing can be added to it, nor any thing taken from it; and God hath so made it, that men should fear before Him. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
That which is hath been long ago, and that which is to be hath already been; and God seeketh that which is pursued. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And moreover I saw under the sun, in the place of justice, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that wickedness was there. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I said in my heart: 'The righteous and the wicked God will judge; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I said in my heart: 'It is because of the sons of men, that God may sift them, and that they may see that they themselves are but as beasts.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them; as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that man hath no preeminence above a beast; for all is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all return to dust. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Who knoweth the spirit of man whether it goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast whether it goeth downward to the earth? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Wherefore I perceived that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his works; for that is his portion; for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him? <span class="anchor"
4: 4 But I returned and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun; and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power, but they had no comforter. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Wherefore I praised the dead that are already dead more than the living that are yet alive; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
but better than they  ​ both is he that hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Again, I considered all labour and all excelling in work, that it is a man's rivalry with his neighbour. This also is vanity and a striving after wind. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The fool foldeth his hands together, And eateth his own flesh. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Better is a handful of quietness, Than both the hands full of labour and striving after wind. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Then I returned and saw vanity under the sun. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

There is one that is alone, and he hath not a second; yea, he hath neither son nor brother; yet is there no end of all his labour, neither is his eye satisfied with riches: 'for whom then do I labour, and bereave my soul of pleasure?' This also is vanity, yea, it is a grievous business. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him that is alone when he falleth, and hath not another to lift him up. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one be warm alone? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And if a man prevail against him that is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king, who knoweth not how to receive admonition any more. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For out of prison he came forth to be king; although in his kingdom he was born poor. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I saw all the living that walk under the sun, that they were with the child, the second, that was to stand up in his stead. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

There was no end of all the people, even of all them whom he did lead; yet they that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a striving after wind. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Guard thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be ready to hearken: it is better than when fools give sacrifices; for they know not that they do evil. <span class="anchor"
5: 5 Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter a word before God; for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth; therefore let thy words be few. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For a dream cometh through a multitude of business; And a fool's voice through a multitude of words. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for He hath no pleasure in fools; pay that which thou vowest. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

Suffer not thy mouth to bring thy flesh into guilt, neither say thou before the messenger, that it was an error; wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thy hands? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For through the multitude of dreams and vanities there are also many words; but fear thou God. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and the violent perverting of justice and righteousness in the state, marvel not at the matter; for one higher than the high watcheth, and there are higher than they. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
But the profit of a land every way is a king that maketh himself servant to the field. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance, with increase; this also is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
When goods increase, they are increased that eat them; and what advantage is there to the owner thereof, saving the beholding of them with his eyes? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Sweet is the sleep of a labouring man, whether he eat little or much;  ​ but the satiety of the rich will not suffer him to sleep. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept by the owner thereof to his hurt; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
and those riches perish by evil adventure; and if he hath begotten a son, there is nothing in his hand. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he go back as he came, and shall take nothing for his labour, which he may carry away in his hand. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And this also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go; and what profit hath he that he laboureth for the wind? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he hath much vexation and sickness and wrath. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

Behold that which I have seen: it is good, yea, it is comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy pleasure for all his labour, wherein he laboureth under the sun, all the days of his life which God hath given him; for this is his portion. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour—this is the gift of God. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For let him remember the days of his life that they are not many; for God answereth him in the joy of his heart. <span class="anchor"
6: 6 There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy upon men: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

a man to whom God giveth riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it; this is vanity, and it is an evil disease. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

If a man beget a hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul have not enough of good, and moreover he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
for it cometh in vanity, and departeth in darkness, and the name thereof is covered with darkness; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
moreover it hath not seen the sun nor known it; this hath gratification rather than the other; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, and enjoy no good; do not all go to one place? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
All the labour of man is for his mouth, And yet the appetite is not filled. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For what advantage hath the wise more than the fool? or the poor man that hath understanding, in walking before the living? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Better is the seeing of the eyes than the wandering of the desire; this also is vanity and a striving after wind. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Whatsoever cometh into being, the name thereof was given long ago, and it is foreknown what man is; neither can he contend with Him that is mightier than he. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Seeing there are many words that increase vanity, what is man the better? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For who knoweth what is good for man in his life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun? <span class="anchor"
7: 7 A good name is better than precious oil; And the day of death than the day of one's birth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
It is better to go to the house of mourning, Than to go to the house of feasting; For that is the end of all men, And the living will lay it to his heart. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Vexation is better than laughter; For by the sadness of the countenance the heart may be gladdened.  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; But the heart of fools is in the house of mirth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, Than for a man to hear the song of fools. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, So is the laughter of the fool; this also is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Surely oppression turneth a wise man into a fool; And a gift destroyeth the understanding. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof; And the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry; For anger resteth in the bosom of fools. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Say not thou: 'How was it that the former days were better than these?' for it is not out of wisdom that thou inquirest concerning this. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Wisdom is good with an inheritance, Yea, a profit to them that see the sun. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For wisdom is a defence, even as money is a defence; but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom preserveth the life of him that hath it. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Consider the work of God; for who can make that straight, which He hath made crooked? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; God hath made even the one as well as the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

All things have I seen in the days of my vanity; there is a righteous man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his evil-doing. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Be not righteous overmuch; neither make thyself overwise; why shouldest thou destroy thyself? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Be not overmuch wicked, neither be thou foolish; why shouldest thou die before thy time? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

It is good that thou shouldest take hold of the one; yea, also from the other withdraw not thy hand; for he that feareth God shall discharge himself of them all. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Wisdom is a stronghold to the wise man more than ten rulers that are in a city. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For there is not a righteous man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Also take not heed unto all words that are spoken, lest thou hear thy servant curse thee; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
for oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
All this have I tried by wisdom; I said: 'I will get wisdom'; but it was far from me. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
That which is is far off, and exceeding deep; who can find it out? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

I turned about, and applied my heart to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the reason of things, and to know wickedness to be folly, and foolishness to be madness; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

and I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands; whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Behold, this have I found, saith Koheleth, adding one thing to another, to find out the account; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
which yet my soul sought, but I found not; one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Behold, this only have I found, that God made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.   ​ <span class="anchor"
8: 8 Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, And the boldness of his face is changed. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
I [counsel thee]: keep the king's command, and that in regard of the oath of God. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Be not hasty to go out of his presence; stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Forasmuch as the king's word hath power; and who may say unto him: 'What doest thou?' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Whoso keepeth the commandment shall know no evil thing; And a wise man's heart discerneth time and judgment. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For to every matter there is a time and judgment; for the evil of man is great upon him. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For he knoweth not that which shall be; for even when it cometh to pass, who shall declare it unto him? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

There is no man that hath power over the wind to retain the wind; neither hath he power over the day of death; and there is no discharge in war; neither shall wickedness deliver him that is given to it. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
All this have I seen, even applied my heart thereto, whatever the work that is done under the sun; what time one man had power over another to his hurt. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And so I saw the wicked buried, and they entered into their rest; but they that had done right went away from the holy place, and were forgotten in the city; this also is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
because a sinner doeth evil a hundred times, and prolongeth his days—though yet I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, that fear before Him; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
but it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow, because he feareth not before God. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

There is a vanity which is done upon the earth: that there are righteous men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there are wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous—I said that this also is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

So I commended mirth, that a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry, and that this should accompany him in his labour all the days of his life which God hath given him under the sun. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth—for neither day nor night do men see sleep with their eyes— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

then I beheld all the work of God, that man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun; because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yea further, though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it. <span class="anchor"
9: 9 For all this I laid to my heart, even to make clear all this: that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God; whether it be love or hatred, man knoweth it not; all is before them. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

All things come alike to all; there is one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth and to him that sacrificeth not; as is the good, so is the sinner, and he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event unto all; yea also, the heart of the sons of men is full of  ​ evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For the living know that they shall die; but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

As well their love, as their hatred and their envy, is long ago perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, And drink thy wine with a merry heart; For God hath already accepted thy works. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let thy garments be always white; And let thy head lack no oil. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

Enjoy life with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which He hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity; for that is thy portion in life, and in thy labour wherein thou labourest under the sun. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Whatsoever thy hand attaineth to do by thy strength, that do; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

For man also knoweth not his time; as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare, even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
This also have I seen as wisdom under the sun, and it seemed great unto me: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
there was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
now there was found in it a man poor and wise, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Then said I: 'Wisdom is better than strength; nevertheless the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The words of the wise spoken in quiet Are more acceptable than the cry of a ruler among fools. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Wisdom is better than weapons of war; But one sinner destroyeth much good. <span class="anchor"
10: 10 Dead flies make the ointment of the perfumer fetid and putrid; So doth a little folly outweigh wisdom and honour. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A wise man's understanding is at his right hand; But a fool's understanding at his left. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Yea also, when a fool walketh by the way, his understanding faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, Leave not thy place; For gentleness allayeth great offences. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, Like an error which proceedeth from a ruler: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Folly is set on great heights, And the rich sit in low place. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I have seen servants upon horses, And princes walking as servants upon the earth.  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; And whoso breaketh through a fence, a serpent shall bite him. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Whoso quarrieth stones shall be hurt therewith; And he that cleaveth wood is endangered thereby. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If the iron be blunt, And one do not whet the edge, Then must he put to more strength; But wisdom is profitable to direct. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If the serpent bite before it is charmed, Then the charmer hath no advantage. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; But the lips of a fool will swallow up himself. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; And the end of his talk is grievous madness. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A fool also multiplieth words; Yet man knoweth not what shall be; And that which shall be after him, Who can tell him? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The labour of fools wearieth every one of them, For he knoweth not how to go to the city. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a boy, And thy princes feast in the morning! <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Happy art thou, O land, when thy king is a free man, And thy princes eat in due season, In strength, and not in drunkenness! <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
By slothfulness the rafters sink in; And through idleness of the hands the house leaketh. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A feast is made for laughter, And wine maketh glad the life; And money answereth all things. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

Curse not the king, no, not in thy thought, And curse not the rich in thy bed-chamber; For a bird of the air shall carry the voice, And that which hath wings shall tell the matter. <span class="anchor"
11: 11 Cast thy bread upon the waters, For thou shalt find it after many days. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Divide a portion into seven, yea, even into eight; For thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

If the clouds be full of rain, They empty themselves upon the earth; And if a tree fall in the south, or in the north, In the place where the tree falleth, there shall it be. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He that observeth the wind shall not sow; And he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

As thou knowest not what is the way of the wind, Nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child; Even so thou knowest not the work of God Who doeth all things. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

In the morning sow thy seed, And in the evening withhold not thy hand; For thou knowest not which shall prosper, whether this or that, Or whether they both shall be alike good. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And the light is sweet, And a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For if a man live many years, Let him rejoice in them all,  ​ And remember the days of darkness, For they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; And let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, And walk in the ways of thy heart, And in the sight of thine eyes; But know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Therefore remove vexation from thy heart, And put away evil from thy flesh; For childhood and youth are vanity. <span class="anchor"
12: 12 Remember then thy Creator in the days of thy youth, Before the evil days come, And the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say: 'I have no pleasure in them'; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Before the sun, and the light, and the moon, And the stars, are darkened, And the clouds return after the rain; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, And the strong men shall bow themselves, And the grinders cease because they are few, And those that look out shall be darkened in the windows, <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

And the doors shall be shut in the street, When the sound of the grinding is low; And one shall start up at the voice of a bird, And all the daughters of music shall be brought low; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, And terrors shall be in the way; And the almond-tree shall blossom, And the grasshopper shall drag itself along, And the caperberry shall fail; Because man goeth to his long home, And the mourners go about the streets; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

Before the silver cord is snapped asunder, And the golden bowl is shattered, And the pitcher is broken at the fountain, And the wheel falleth shattered, into the pit; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And the dust returneth to the earth as it was, And the spirit returneth unto God who gave it. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Vanity of vanities, saith Koheleth; all is vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And besides that Koheleth was wise, he also taught the people knowledge; yea, he pondered, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Koheleth sought to find out words of delight, and that which was written uprightly, even words of truth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails well fastened are those that are composed in collections; they are given from one shepherd. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God, and keep His commandments; for this is the whole man. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

For God shall bring every work into the judgment concerning every hidden thing, whether it be good or whether it be evil. The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God, and keep His Commandments; for this is the whole man.
